questions.stem: This question is about elements, compounds and mixtures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the element that burns with a lilac flame.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name the technique used to separate the mixture of colours in black ink.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The box gives the names of some substances. Choose substances from the box to answer these questions.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Identify the compound.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Identify the mixture.

parts.label: c-iii

questions.stem: Crude oil is a mixture of hydrocarbons.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the process used to separate crude oil into fractions.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one use of the kerosene fraction.

parts.label: c
parts.text: One of the hydrocarbons in the refinery gas fraction is an alkane with the structural formula $ \mathrm{C H_{3} C H_{2} C H_{2} C H_{3}} $

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Give the name of this alkane.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Calculate the relative molecular mass $ ( M_{\mathrm{r}}) $ of this alkane.

parts.label: d
parts.text: One of the alkanes in the gasoline fraction has the displayed formula

parts.label: d-i
parts.text: Determine the molecular formula of this alkane.

parts.label: d-ii
parts.text: Give the general formula for the alkanes.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Catalytic cracking is used to convert long-chain alkanes into shorter-chain alkanes.

parts.label: e-i
parts.text: Name the catalyst used in catalytic cracking.

parts.label: e-ii
parts.text: Explain why it is necessary to convert long-chain alkanes into shorter-chain alkanes.

parts.label: f
parts.text: Catalytic cracking also produces alkenes. $ \mathrm{C}_{1 1} \mathrm{H}_{2 4} $ can undergo cracking to give pentane $ \left( \mathrm{C}_{5} \mathrm{H}_{1 2} \right) $ and two different alkenes. Complete the equation for this cracking reaction. $\mathrm {C} _ {1 1} \mathrm {H} _ {2 4} \rightarrow \mathrm {C} _ {5} \mathrm {H} _ {1 2} +$

questions.stem: This question is about copper and its compounds.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Copper is a metal used for electrical wiring. Explain why copper is a good conductor of electricity.

parts.label: b
parts.text: This apparatus is used to investigate the electrolysis of copper(II) sulfate solution with graphite electrodes. Copper forms at the negative electrode and oxygen forms at the positive electrode.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: State what would be observed at each electrode. negative electrode positive electrode ..

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: The ionic half-equation for the reaction at the negative electrode is $\mathrm {C u} ^ {2 +} + 2 \mathrm {e} ^ {-} \rightarrow \mathrm {C u}$ State why this is a reduction reaction.

parts.label: b-iii
parts.text: Explain why the copper(II) sulfate solution becomes paler blue during the electrolysis. (2)

parts.label: c
parts.text: When hydrated copper(II) sulfate crystals are heated, anhydrous copper(II) sulfate forms. A mass of 12.5 g of hydrated copper(II) sulfate crystals is heated in a crucible until all the water of crystallisation is removed. A mass of 8.0 g of anhydrous copper(II) sulfate forms. Show by calculation that the formula of hydrated copper(II) sulfate is $ \mathrm{C u S O_{4}. 5 H_{2}O} $ $[ M _ {\mathrm {r}} \mathrm {o f C u S O} _ {4} = 1 5 9. 5 \quad M _ {\mathrm {r}} \mathrm {o f H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} = 1 8 ]$

questions.stem: A student investigates the reaction between sodium hydroxide solution and dilute sulfuric acid. He does a titration to find the concentration of the sulfuric acid. This is his plan for the titration. There are some mistakes and omissions in his plan. rinse a conical flask with the sodium hydroxide solution use a measuring cylinder to measure out $ 2 5 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of the sodium hydroxide solution and add it to the conical flask add a few drops of methyl orange indicator to the conical flask rinse a burette with water and then fill it with the sulfuric acid add the acid from the burette to the conical flask until the indicator changes colour at the end-point of the titration record the final burette reading

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give the colour change of the methyl orange indicator at the end-point.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe four changes that the student could make to improve his plan. He finds that $ 1 6. 7 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of the dilute sulfuric acid neutralises $ 2 5. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of sodium hydroxide solution of concentration $ 0. 2 0 0 \mathrm{m o l} / \mathrm{d m}^{3} $

parts.label: c
parts.text: The student then does the titration correctly. The equation for the reaction is $2 \mathrm {N a O H} + \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {S O} _ {4} \rightarrow \mathrm {N a} _ {2} \mathrm {S O} _ {4} + 2 \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O}$ Calculate the concentration, in mol/dm $ ^{3} $ , of the sulfuric acid. $\mathrm {m o l / d m ^ {3}}$

questions.stem: Oxygen can be prepared from hydrogen peroxide using a catalyst.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Which is a correct statement about oxygen? A it burns with a squeaky pop B it relights a glowing splint C it turns blue litmus red D it turns limewater milky

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain how a catalyst increases the rate of a reaction.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The equation for the preparation of oxygen from hydrogen peroxide is $2 \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} _ {2} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} + \mathrm {O} _ {2}$ This equation can also be written using displayed formulae to show all the covalent bonds in the molecules. $2 H - O - O - H \rightarrow 2 H - O - H + O = O$ The table gives the bond energies for these bonds.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Use the values in the table to calculate the enthalpy change, $ \Delta H $ , for the reaction. Include a sign in your answer.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Complete the energy level diagram to show the position of the products and the enthalpy change, $ \Delta H $ , for the reaction.

questions.stem: Ethanol, $ \mathrm{C_{2} H_{5} O H} $ , can be manufactured from ethene and steam using a phosphoric acid catalyst. (a) (i) State the temperature and pressure used in this manufacturing process. temperature pressure ... (ii) Draw the displayed formula of ethanol.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Ethanol burns in a plentiful supply of air to form carbon dioxide and water.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Give the chemical equation for this reaction.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: When the air supply is limited, incomplete combustion occurs and carbon monoxide forms. State why carbon monoxide is poisonous to humans.

parts.label: c
parts.text: When ethanol reacts with ethanoic acid, an ester forms. Give the name of this ester.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Butanedioic acid and ethanediol react together to form a polyester and water.

parts.label: d-i
parts.text: Give the name of this type of polymerisation.

parts.label: d-ii
parts.text: Complete the equation. Show only one repeat unit of the polyester.

questions.stem: This question is about some Group 2 elements and their compounds.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calcium reacts with water to produce calcium hydroxide and hydrogen gas.

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: Give the word equation for this reaction.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: State two observations that would be made during this reaction.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe how a pure, dry sample of the insoluble salt, barium sulfate, could be made from the two solids sodium sulfate and barium chloride.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Give an ionic equation for the reaction that occurs. Include state symbols in your equation.

parts.label: c
parts.text: When magnesium nitrate is heated, magnesium oxide, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen form. The equation for the reaction is $2 \mathrm {M g} \left(\mathrm {N O} _ {3}\right) _ {2} (\mathrm {s}) \rightarrow 2 \mathrm {M g O} (\mathrm {s}) + 4 \mathrm {N O} _ {2} (\mathrm {g}) + \mathrm {O} _ {2} (\mathrm {g})$

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: What is the name for this type of reaction? A addition B combustion decomposition D neutralisation

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Calculate the total volume, in $ \mathrm{d m}^{3} $ of gas produced at rtp when 7.7 g of magnesium nitrate completely reacts. [Assume that the molar volume of a gas at rtp is $ 2 4 \mathrm{d m}^{3} $] [ $ M_{\mathrm{r}} $ of $ \mathrm{M g(N O_{3})_{2}}=1 4 8 $] Give your answer to two significant figures.
